text:
Michael Brandsegg-Nygard said all summer his only goal was making the Red Wings (Yahoo Sports). He made it, and Detroit Hockey Now says he's leading the team's rookies. He's 21, a Norwegian taken 15th in 2024, with ten points in 18 games at more than 15 minutes a night.

The underlying play is better than the scoring. Detroit has 58% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, nearly seven points better than without him. He has three goals on 6.0 expected, so he's been unlucky finishing, though the Red Wings have scored 5.6 more goals than expected around him.

His best night was Nov 2 in Florida: a goal and an assist in a 5-3 win. On a Detroit team without Dylan Larkin, who is refusing to play until he's traded, a rookie who drives play matters more than usual. The closest comparable picks in our draft history include Matthew Wood. Our projection sees about 17 goals.
